clue.text: Option when tumble-drier's broken? Relax

blocks.note: first meaning, taken literally: peg every bit of the washing out on the line
second meaning: an idiom for behaving without inhibition

explanation.surface: A household with a broken dryer weighs its options, then is told to calm down.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the first half is a playful literal reading of the idiom: with no dryer, all the laundry goes on the washing line.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to drop all restraint and be completely uninhibited, which is a strong form of relaxing.

clue.text: Jenny possibly entertained by stories for girls in Balamory?

indicators.note: a guest entertained is taken in and held within, so the donkey word sits inside

blocks.note: stories in the sense of untruths
a jenny is a female donkey, an example of an ass

explanation.surface: A girl called Jenny is being read tales aimed at the youngsters of a children's TV town.
explanation.walkthrough: Jenny looks like a girl's name; it is a female donkey. Balamory is a children's TV show set on a Scottish island, which is why the Scots word for girls fits.
explanation.definitionFit: Lassie is the Scottish word for a girl, so girls in a Scottish setting are the plural.

clue.text: Prepare to drive sheep around empty enclosure

indicators.note: the sheep word goes round the outside of the other letters, surrounding them
emptying a word removes its contents, keeping only its two ends

blocks.note: a tup is a ram
first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A farmer gets ready to herd sheep round a vacant pen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drive' suggests herding livestock, but it is the golfer's long first shot.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf you place the ball on a peg before striking off from the tee, so the phrase means getting ready to hit.

clue.text: I got them to fly around river in biplane

indicators.note: letters sent flying scatter and land in a new order
the jumbled letters are wrapped about the river letter, enclosing it

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of having persuaded others to take to the air along a river in an old aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: The de Havilland Tiger Moth is a famous 1930s British biplane used for pilot training.

clue.text: Prisoners hoarding extremely dim adult publications

indicators.note: to hoard is to keep stored away inside, so these letters hold the others
the extremes of a word are its first and last letters only

blocks.note: lags are convicts, especially old hands
first and last letters of the word
A is the old film-classification abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: Inmates stashing away rather dim-witted pornography.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Adult publications' reads as one phrase, but adult only supplies a letter. Lads' mags are British men's lifestyle magazines like Loaded and FHM.
explanation.definitionFit: Lad mags are a genre of magazine aimed at young men, so they are a kind of periodical.

clue.text: Home ground, where not much stops bowler?

indicators.note: a stopper sits inside an opening, so these letters plug the middle of the hat word

blocks.note: a bowler is a round felt hat
a bit means a small amount

explanation.surface: A cricket question: at the home ground, where does a little something halt the bowler?
explanation.walkthrough: Home ground and bowler conjure cricket, but the bowler is headwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitat is the natural environment where an animal or plant lives, its home territory.

clue.text: Approaches one bar, as missing all starters

indicators.note: every word loses its opening letter, as a meal without its first courses

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone heads to a pub where, as it happens, there are no first courses on the menu.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starters' suggests food; here it means the first letter of each of the three words.
explanation.definitionFit: To near something is to come closer to it, a synonym of approach in the third-person verb form.

clue.text: Spouse's alternative beer?

blocks.note: the other option is the alternative one
a half is a half-pint of beer

explanation.surface: Asking what a husband or wife's substitute drink might be.
explanation.walkthrough: In a British pub 'a half' means half a pint of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Your other half is an informal idiom for your husband, wife or partner.

clue.text: Time Italian restaurant served up mayonnaise

indicators.note: in a down entry, being sent up means the letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: an era is a period of time
trat is a short informal form of trattoria

explanation.surface: At a certain hour an Italian eatery brought out a creamy sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: Tartare sauce is mayonnaise mixed with capers, gherkins and herbs, a flavoured kind of that dressing.

clue.text: Had a go at playing cricket?

definitions.text: Had a go at playing cricket?

blocks.clueFragment: Had a go at playing cricket?
blocks.note: surface reading: tried one's hand at the game
setter's reading: verbally attacked, as fielders do to a batsman to put him off

explanation.surface: Someone tried their hand at cricket for the first time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Had a go at' looks like 'attempted'; it means 'taunted'. In cricket, the practice of fielders insulting a batter is called sledging.
explanation.definitionFit: Sledging is cricket slang for abusive taunts aimed at an opponent, so the past tense means verbally attacked during play.

clue.text: British stew, rabbit

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for British
being in a stew or a lather both mean a state of agitation

explanation.surface: A British dish of stewed rabbit.
explanation.walkthrough: Stew and rabbit suggest a casserole. To rabbit (on) is British slang for chattering at length.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean to talk on and on foolishly; rabbit is informal British slang for chatter.

clue.text: Bring in American books of value

blocks.note: to import is to bring goods in from abroad
A is the abbreviation for American
NT, the New Testament, is a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Advice to import valuable American books.
explanation.definitionFit: Something of value carries weight or significance, and that is what the adjective means.

clue.text: Going around spacious southern country

indicators.note: turning around means facing the other way, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: an airy room is open and roomy
S is the abbreviation for southern

explanation.surface: A traveller tours a large country in the south.
explanation.definitionFit: Syria is a nation in the Middle East, on the eastern Mediterranean coast.

clue.text: Hotel about to fill drinks and water bottles

indicators.note: filling means going inside, so these letters sit within the drinks word

blocks.note: sips are small drinks
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
on as in 'on the subject of'

explanation.surface: A hotel is about to stock up on drinks and bottled water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to' reads as 'going to', but the two words are split.
explanation.definitionFit: A soda siphon is a pressurised bottle for dispensing fizzy water.

clue.text: Odd misnomer associated with soft fruit

indicators.note: an odd thing is strange or out of order, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for soft
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A strange wrong name has become attached to a squashy fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soft fruit' reads as one phrase, but soft only supplies the musical letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The persimmon is an orange tomato-like fruit, also called sharon fruit or kaki.

clue.text: Something to eat from Spooner's harbour catch

indicators.note: Rev. Spooner was famous for swapping the opening sounds of words

blocks.note: a quay is a harbour wharf, a take is a catch; swap their opening sounds

explanation.surface: A fisherman's catch in Spooner's harbour yields a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: Quay is pronounced 'key', so swapping the K and T sounds gives the snack.
explanation.definitionFit: A teacake is a light sweet bun with dried fruit, usually toasted and buttered: a snack.

clue.text: Fix piece for television presenter

blocks.note: to anchor is to fix firmly in place
a piece in chess or draughts is a man

explanation.surface: A repair part is needed for a TV host.
explanation.definitionFit: An anchorman is the main presenter who links a news broadcast together.

clue.text: Pretentiousness in Zeppelin, perhaps

blocks.note: putting on airs is acting superior
in and hip both mean fashionable

explanation.surface: There is affectation in a rock band, Led Zeppelin perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link to Zeppelin but is the fashionable word.
explanation.definitionFit: A Zeppelin is a rigid dirigible, an example of a lighter-than-air craft, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Follower's online comment inspired by boundless Dales

indicators.note: something inspired is breathed in, so these letters are taken inside
without bounds means losing its edges, the first and last letters

blocks.note: taken as written
a post is a message on a forum or social site

explanation.surface: A fan writes something on the internet after visiting the wide-open Yorkshire Dales.
explanation.definitionFit: The apostles were the twelve disciples of Jesus, so an apostle is a devoted adherent.

clue.text: Rubber disc is hard and liable to do someone a mischief!

definitions.text: liable to do someone a mischief!

blocks.note: the puck in ice hockey is a hard rubber disc
taken as written
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A hard rubber hockey disc could hurt somebody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do someone a mischief' is an idiom for injuring them, matching the hockey picture, but the answer means playfully naughty, after Puck the sprite.
explanation.definitionFit: Puck is the mischievous sprite of A Midsummer Night's Dream, so the adjective describes someone prone to pranks.

clue.text: Considerate, cut fat off crown of lamb

indicators.note: meat that has gone off is spoiled, so these letters are disordered
the crown is the top, which in a word is its first letter

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A thoughtful butcher trims the fat from a crown roast of lamb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut fat off crown of lamb' reads as butchery; crown of lamb is a real roast, which disguises the first-letter device.
explanation.definitionFit: Being considerate means showing sensitivity to others' feelings, which is what a person with tact does.

clue.text: Supported by mate at first, truant lost temper

indicators.note: something lost has gone astray, so these letters wander into a new order
only the initial letter of the preceding word is wanted
in a down entry, being supported means sitting on top of the other part

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Backed up by a friend at first, a skiving pupil flew into a rage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost temper' looks like a verb phrase, but lost works on the word before and temper alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A temper, as in a fit of temper, is an angry outburst, the same as a tantrum.

clue.text: Sweep left river creature close to Sooty

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is used

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left
the otter lives along rivers
last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Sweep, the puppet dog, abandoned a river animal near Sooty.
explanation.walkthrough: Sooty and Sweep are a famous British TV glove-puppet bear and dog, so Sweep looks like a character, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweep, short for sweepstake, is a draw in which prizes go to names picked at random.

clue.text: Think duck is by tree

blocks.note: a duck is a score of nought in cricket, shaped like the letter
the pine is a conifer

explanation.surface: Someone reckons a duck is near a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: To opine is to state or hold an opinion, a formal word for believing something.

clue.text: Tests duplex Amsterdam houses

indicators.note: to house is to contain, so the phrase holds the answer within it

blocks.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: Inspectors check out two-storey homes in the Dutch capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'houses' looks like a noun, as in buildings, but it is the verb meaning contains.
explanation.definitionFit: Exams are examinations, formal assessments of knowledge such as school tests.

clue.text: Frauds social worker checks on X, for example

blocks.note: cons are swindles
taken as written
the ant is a social insect and a worker caste, a common crossword pun

explanation.surface: A council employee investigates swindlers on behalf of an anonymous X.
explanation.walkthrough: 'social worker' suggests a welfare officer; it is the insect. The worker comes after the other parts, holding back the on, which is the sense of checks.
explanation.definitionFit: X is a letter that is not a vowel, so it is an example of that class of letters.

clue.text: Dart that's fine, but not new

indicators.note: but not means excluding, so the named letter is taken away

blocks.note: fine as in thin or slender
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Someone judges a dart as fine, though not brand new.
explanation.definitionFit: A dart is a small pointed missile thrown or fired, which is what an arrow is.

clue.text: Pest getting into beat, beginning to imitate drums

indicators.note: to get into something is to go inside it
only the start of the next word is wanted, its first letter

blocks.note: to tan someone's hide is to beat them
an imp is a mischievous child, a little pest
first letter of the word

explanation.surface: An annoying child starts to copy a rhythm on the drums.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beat' and 'drums' point to rhythm, but beat means thrash here.
explanation.definitionFit: Timpani are kettledrums, the large tuned drums of an orchestra.

clue.text: Feelings of guilt concerning detective

blocks.note: re means regarding
Inspector Morse is the Oxford detective of Colin Dexter's novels and the TV series

explanation.surface: Someone feels guilty about a detective.
explanation.definitionFit: Remorse is deep regret for wrongdoing, a sense of guilt and contrition.

clue.text: Writer, reportedly serious, may whinge when bothered

indicators.note: reports are spoken, so the word is wanted for how it sounds, not its spelling
being bothered means being stirred up, so these letters are agitated into a new order

blocks.note: earnest means serious, and the first name sounds the same
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An author, said to be a solemn type, is apt to complain when annoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: Oscar Wilde's play The Importance of Being Earnest turns on the same sound pairing.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernest Hemingway was the American novelist of The Old Man and the Sea and A Farewell to Arms.
